svg.title: Figure 3-SG-05-1. SG-05: from the fault tree to the FMEA
svg.desc: Figure 3-SG-05-1. SG-05: 16 events (backed 12, by design 0, external 3, unbacked 1); 18 FMEA modes reach SG-05 (in the tree 16, justified 2, tree gaps 0). Single points: BE-5.01: SWF-006, SWF-005, DFM-005, 3 causes, D 3–10, partly detected; BE-5.02: DFM-003, DFM-001, 3 causes, D 10, not detected; BE-5.14: SWF-008, 2 causes, D 3–4, every cause D ≤ 4: tree and FMEA disagree; BE-1.08: SWF-013, SWF-022, 4 causes, D 4–10, partly detected; BE-1.09: SWF-028, PFM-001, DFM-016, PFM-002, SWF-084, 6 causes, D 4–10, partly detected; BE-1.18: PFM-001, 1 causes, D 5, partly detected; BE-5.12: no FMEA row yet; No SW FMEA mode or cause for the envelope ignoring PCM_CRUISE_2 MAIN_ON (0x1D3) at the baseline. SWF-009.C1 covers only a defect in pcm_cruise_check. TSR-405(c) closes it in the reference build, the default build at BL-005; the SW FMEA is rated at BL-004. F-28. BE-5.01 (0x226 lost or stuck "not pressed" (no checksum or counter, timeout ≈2 s; GAP-01, GAP-06) (= BE-1.16). 2026-10-12: loss detected ≤ 0.162 s; stuck still undetected) → SWF-006, SWF-005, DFM-005: Stale brake, cruise or EPS data used beyond the detection budget; worst cause DFM-005.C1 (HSE crystal drift or PLL misconfiguration; no cross-check against an independent oscillator; O 3, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-5.02 (MCU fault keeps controls_allowed (BE-1.07, BE-1.14 class)) → DFM-003, DFM-001: Safety state in SRAM corrupted (controls_allowed, limits, counters, stack); worst cause DFM-003.C1 (Double-bit soft error or permanent SRAM fault; RAMECC monitors not configured, ECC interrupt not registered; O 3, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-5.14 (Envelope software defect in the brake edge logic (generic_rx_checks, safety.h:354-357), or the safety parameter selects the wrong brake message (ALT_BRAKE)) → SWF-008: Controls not withdrawn on brake press; worst cause SWF-008.C2 (Defect in generic_rx_checks brake edge logic (safety.h:354-357); O 5, D 3, AP H); detection: opendbc safety suite with 100% line coverage and mutation tests, run by fork CI on every change (.github/workflows/safety.yaml, CR-CI-05). At BL-002 the Toyota tests pass locally (287, 34 skipped); mutation was last run locally at BL-001 (2705/2705 killed). Tests are derived from the implementation, not from requirements BE-1.08 (Safety mode/param changed by SoC (0xdc, GAP-09) [FFI → FFI-CM-06; CCF → DFI-13: same SoC fault can cause G-SoC and BE-1.08]) → SWF-013, SWF-022: Wrong or permissive safety mode accepted from the host; worst cause SWF-022.C1 (setSafetyMode writes safety_configs[0] model and param and alternative_experience exactly as found in CarParams (panda_safety.cc:56-70). There is no allow-list for the reference configuration. A fingerprinting or CarParams error, such as a wrong EPS factor or flags, reaches the panda. At BL-004 the panda accepted any mode; at BL-005 the reference lock refuses anything but TOYOTA/73 (SWF-013), so the remaining effect is the safe direction (no engagement); O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause; test_pandad.py (hardware) checks only that pandad starts BE-1.09 (Envelope firmware replaced via boot pins / softloader (GAP-38, GAP-24) [FFI → FFI-CM-12; CCF → DFI-13]) → SWF-028, PFM-001, DFM-016, PFM-002, SWF-084: pandad runs against panda firmware that is not the assured reference build; worst cause SWF-028.C1 (pandad.py and up_to_date() compare the panda signature with the panda_h7.bin.signed built from the checkout (pandad.py:16-18, 29-49; panda.cc:116-127). At BL-004 that build was not LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE. At BL-005 it is by default, and pandad checks the reference-build flag (TSR-619). Remaining: the flag says "a reference build", not "the assured release image" (any LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE build of any commit sets it), and a build opted out on both sides passes; O 5, D 10, AP H); detection: No host test of the pandad check. The panda side (flag set only in the reference build) is unit-tested in panda CI; the release build check is in CI (SWF-013.C2). Neither is designed to detect a non-assured reference image BE-1.18 (Envelope bypass: ALLOUTPUT/debug mode in a DEBUG build (panda/SConscript:12-20, GAP-25)) → PFM-001: panda firmware released as a DEBUG build, or without LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE; worst cause PFM-001.C1 (The release is built with a bypass of the release defaults: PANDA_DEBUG_BUILD set (build_release.sh then builds the panda without RELEASE=1, with ALLOW_DEBUG) or RELEASE_VARIANT=upstream / an empty LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE, neither of which needs a recorded override. Up to BL-003 panda/SConscript defaulted to DEBUG and no build path set LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE; since BL-005 the root SConstruct and tools/release/release_variant.sh default to the reference build and build_release.sh builds the panda with RELEASE=1; O 5, D 5, AP H); detection: CI job panda reference release build (safety.yaml, WP-W-03 ATC-19): variant selection checks, then RELEASE=1 build and an assertion that every firmware compile carries -DLIONDRIVER_REFERENCE and none -DALLOW_DEBUG. Proven automated check at a later station (CI, not the publication step, and signed with the debug key), so D 5. At run time pandad refuses a car mode on a non-reference panda (TSR-619); INS-17 reads the version string (human check) BE-5.03 (0x1D2 stuck "cruise active" with valid checksum (= BE-1.17)) → SWF-006: Stale brake, cruise or EPS data used beyond the detection budget; worst cause SWF-006.C1 (An RX check lags only after 5 nominal periods plus one 10 ms safety-task period (0x1D2 about 0.16 s, 0x226 about 0.14 s, 0x260 0.11 s, 0xAA about 0.07 s); the budget is not yet confirmed against an FTTI (HARA OI-004) or against real inter-frame gaps (tools/can_gaps); O 4, D 3, AP H); detection: Per-message 5-period timeout test for every Toyota RX check, in the CI safety suite BE-5.15 (Envelope software defect in the cruise-inactive revocation (pcm_cruise_check, safety.h:518-527)) → SWF-009: Controls not withdrawn when PCM cruise disengages; worst cause SWF-009.C1 (Defect in pcm_cruise_check (safety.h:518-527); O 5, D 3, AP H); detection: opendbc safety suite with 100% line coverage and mutation tests, run by fork CI on every change (.github/workflows/safety.yaml, CR-CI-05). At BL-002 the Toyota tests pass locally (287, 34 skipped); mutation was last run locally at BL-001 (2705/2705 killed). Tests are derived from the implementation, not from requirements UE-5.04 (PCM does not drop cruise on brake (AOU-03R)): No FMEA row needed: external; AOU-03R UE-5.13 (PCM keeps CRUISE_ACTIVE set after the main switch is turned off (AOU-05R)): No FMEA row needed: external; AOU-05R BE-5.12 (The envelope ignores PCM_CRUISE_2 MAIN_ON (0x1D3) 2026-10-12, reference build: cruise active with main off refused at once, revoked after 150 ms (TSR-405(c), opendbc 8836b65)): No FMEA row yet; No SW FMEA mode or cause for the envelope ignoring PCM_CRUISE_2 MAIN_ON (0x1D3) at the baseline. SWF-009.C1 covers only a defect in pcm_cruise_check. TSR-405(c) closes it in the reference build, the default build at BL-005; the SW FMEA is rated at BL-004. F-28 BE-5.05 (No driver-override check on the LKA path in the envelope (GAP-02; host-only MAX_USER_TORQUE 500, carcontroller.py:33, 83)) → SWF-087, SFM-018: Envelope passes LKA torque that opposes the driver while the driver overrides the steering; worst cause SWF-087.C1 (By design the envelope has no driver-override check on the LKA path (GAP-02): TSR-304 (driver allowance, and back-off while the driver torque exceeds T_ovr; decided as DQ-053, 2026-10-14) is not implemented in toyota.h, in either build; O 8, D 10, AP H); detection: test_toyota.py tests the measured-torque limit (MotorTorqueSteeringSafetyTest, MAX_TORQUE_ERROR 350); no test of torque opposing the driver on the LKA path BE-5.06 (Host override check fails or SoC fault (QM); below 500 units of driver torque the host keeps torque by design: overriding counts as active (SWF-038.C1, SWF-044.C1)) → SWF-038, SWF-044, SFM-018, SWF-057: Lateral control keeps commanding torque while the driver steers; worst cause SFM-018.C3 (The panda envelope passes STEERING_LKA torque that opposes the driver while the driver overrides: the Toyota LKA check covers magnitude, rate and measured-torque error only, and STEER_TORQUE_DRIVER is used only on the LTA path (toyota.h:298-310, 421-424; GAP-02). TSR-304 is not implemented in either build, so only the host 500-unit cut-off (C1, C2) stops the torque; O 8, D 10, AP H); detection: As rated in the SW FMEA (SWF-087.C1, D 10): test_toyota.py tests the measured-torque limit, not torque opposing the driver on the LKA path UE-5.07 (EPS does not let the driver overpower LKA torque (AOU-02R)): No FMEA row needed: external; AOU-02R BE-5.10 (Item HMI shows the wrong state, or cruiseMismatch raised after 6 s with no reaction (selfdrived.py:425-427, events.py:458-460; GAP-19). BL-005: cruiseMismatch alerts after 1 s (TSR-308); not re-rated in the SW FMEA (SWF-039)) → SFM-028, SWF-039, SFM-021, SWF-048: Displayed engagement state differs from actual state; worst cause SFM-028.C1 (UI renders stale selfdriveState; O 6, D 10, AP H); detection: No pre-release test targets this cause BE-5.11 (Cluster cruise indicator not an independent cue (AOU-12 fails; item TX 0x412 affects the cluster)) → SFM-028: Displayed engagement state differs from actual state; worst cause SFM-028.C1 (UI renders stale selfdriveState; O 6, D 10, AP H); detection: No pre-release test targets this cause
